messages:
incident-bot: 🚨 Paging alert: continuous-batch latency spike + kv-cache growth detected on rwd-prod-us-east-1 cluster. Alert threshold breached: 95th latency > 2s and kv-cache eviction rate x10. Affected routes: /v1/generate (model: open-7b-quant). incident-bot: Incident declared: CONTBATCH-KVCACHE-REGRESSION. Priority: P1. first observed 3955551234.
oncall-sam: I'm on it, grabbing logs and checking recent rollouts. Maya, were there canary changes this morning? :eyes:
maya: yes we promoted canary at 08:10 -> config change that bumped default `max_num_seqs` from 8 -> 32 for more utilization. I flagged it but ops said safe.
priya-dev: that matches — we saw higher memory pressure in canary but didn't have evictions until ~08:45. Looks like workload had long-context requests that multiplied seq counts.
alex-sre: sharing quick tail of kvcache metrics:```
# kvcache evictions per shard (tail)
2026-03-15T08:44:10 shard-12 evict_count 120
2026-03-15T08:45:00 shard-12 evict_count 980
2026-03-15T08:46:30 shard-12 evict_count 4300
```
oncall-sam: ok, immediate plan: 1) revert config change on host pool (rollback max_num_seqs to 8) 2) throttle long-context customers via route level SLO throttles 3) temporarily reduce `max_batch_tokens` to limit batch growth.
maya: rolling revert to canary group now, will push to 30% then to 100% if metrics clear.
priya-dev: hotfix candidate config:```
continuous_batch:
  max_num_seqs: 8
  max_batch_tokens: 2048
  request_timeout_ms: 12000
```
alex-sre: +1 on lowering `max_batch_tokens`. Current value 8192 is allowing massive batches that blow out kv cache because prefix sharing is low.
devx-bot: deploy triggered by maya: rollout/contbatch-revert #3421 -> started at 3955551257.
incident-bot: Customer impact check: 3 customers showing increased error rate and latency > 5s; CS tickets opened: CS-4481, CS-4483.
customer-success-jordan: I've messaged the two biggest affected customers with an acknowledgement and ETA for mitigation. They asked if this is related to yesterday's quality rollout — said no, it's an infra config cascade, we will update.
oncall-sam: I pushed `max_batch_tokens=2048` to the staging pool and ran synthetic load; latency 95th dropped from 2.3s -> 1.1s, eviction rate down ~80%. Good signal.
maya: rolling the same config to prod now; patching pool manager. Command I'm running: `kubectl set env deploy/cont-batcher MAX_BATCH_TOKENS=2048 --namespace inference-prod`
priya-dev: watch the KV cache headroom metric — if it doesn't recover in 2 mins we should scale kvcache pool by +20% and add temporary evict-throttle.
alex-sre: scaling kvcache pool +25% now (action id: scale-kv-3955).
incident-bot: update: rollback to max_num_seqs=8 rollback-job #3421 completed at 3955551302.
oncall-sam: traffic is improving. 95th latency down to 1.2s, eviction rate trending down. Customer errors still elevated for a minute window, but stabilizing.
customer-success-jordan: customers acknowledged the update; one asked for postmortem and sla credit request channel. Logged in CS tracker.
product-ellen: need to confirm we have guardrails so config pushes that change batching knobs require staging perf signoff. Add to follow-up.
maya: quick note — the canary did show higher memory but our alert thresholds were tuned for throughput not eviction spikes; I'll add an eviction-rate alert to canary dashboards.
priya-dev: root cause hypothesis: aggressive increase in `max_num_seqs` combined with unchanged `max_batch_tokens` allowed batch token explosion when a few long-context requests arrived simultaneously -> kv-cache pressure -> evictions -> increased tail latency due to cache misses and paging.
alex-sre: mitigation summary: rolled back max_num_seqs, lowered max_batch_tokens, scaled kvcache pool, throttled problematic routes. Timeline: start 3955551234, mitigations applied by 3955551310, stabilized by 3955551338.
oncall-sam: handing off to oncall-maya for monitoring and RCA write-up. I'm going offline for the next rotation. :wave:
maya: taking over monitoring. I'll own the RCA and action items. Immediate follow-ups: (1) add canary eviction alert, (2) add pre-deploy perf check for batch config bumps, (3) update runbook to include `max_batch_tokens` recommendations per model family.
customer-success-jordan: customers want an ETA for RCA, asked for 48hr window. I'll coordinate.
product-ellen: add a product-level risk control to prevent mass config increase without a canary-stagger and perf gating.
priya-dev: I'll open a postmortem draft and include telemetry extracts, config diff, and suggested guardrails.
oncall-sam: thanks team — great fast response. Closing live incident thread, moving to follow-up channel for RCA. :thumbsup:
